post_port_changes.change: Removed from this build context. The port carried the dmac-assistant clone's root baml_src/ as a hand-kept copy of NessieAI/dmac_assistant/baml_src/ (byte-identical, all 8 files). The Dockerfile now COPYs the Compose named context dmac_assistant_baml, which docker-compose.yml maps onto NessieAI/dmac_assistant/baml_src/, to the same /app/baml_src/, so baml-cli generate and the generators' output_dir put the judge client at /app/tools/e2e/baml_client/ as before.

post_port_changes.change: Removed from this build context, with its context_file_inventory entry. The cc-agent image no longer bakes any graph-schema capture. The agent gets the graph's schema from the nextseek-graph-schema op (registered in NessieAI/cc/op_registry/ops.py), which calls POST /nextseek_api/assistant/graph-schema/; that reads the live Neo4j catalog through chat_nextseek's graph_catalog, renders it with graph_context, and falls back to the committed NessieAI/chat_nextseek/src/chat_nextseek/context/neo4j_schema.json -- naming the fallback and the reason -- when the graph cannot serve the catalog. min_graph_schema.json stays baked and unchanged: despite the name it is hand-authored routing prose, not a capture.
post_port_changes.why: Measured 2026-09-17: this file's own fetched_at read 2026-04-23 and the chat_nextseek copy's 2026-08-21, while the deployed graph was at schema 1.2. Neither described it -- neither named the Attribute, Project, Person, GraphMeta or OrphanSample labels or the source_hash / project_ids / search_text / synced_at properties, and the chat_nextseek copy still listed CHILD_OF, a relationship type the graph work deleted. A capture baked into an image cannot be kept in step with a synced graph, and nothing told the agent it was stale. Nessie master plan 2026-09-17, task 7.3.

The generated capabilities-copy block of the Dockerfile now COPYs each canonical file from the Compose named context chat_nextseek, after the plugin COPY, to the same /app/plugins/nextseek/context/ path, so the image holds the same eleven context files. Five of the six were byte-identical to their canonical twin, so the image bytes are unchanged. capabilities.md had drifted (the ported copy lacks a Publication entry), but the image already took the canonical file through the named-context COPY, so its image bytes are unchanged too. The plugin tree keeps MANIFEST.md, ops.json, read_safe_endpoints.json and the two graph snapshots min_graph_schema.json and neo4j_schema.json, which differ from their canonical twins and stay in context_file_inventory. (neo4j_schema.json was removed on 2026-09-17; see the entry above.)
post_port_changes.why: NessieAI consolidation Phase C: one copy of each plugin context file, so nobody keeps two copies identical by hand.

post_port_changes.change: Three POSTs left the read-safe list, byte-identical in both copies (NessieAI/ns/read_safe_endpoints.json, which the write gate enforces, and this baked copy): /nextseek_api/batch-upload/validate/, /nextseek_api/data_files/download/ and /nextseek_api/sops/download/. The write gate let api-read ask for them, but the REST tool every api-read ends in (tool_nextseek_api_request in chat_nextseek's helpers/tools/nextseek_api.py) allows only the POSTs in its own _READ_POST_PATHS, so each answered 200 with a nested ok:false 'Write operations are not permitted'. The skill (skills/nextseek/SKILL.md) and the manifest (context/MANIFEST.md) no longer promise downloads or workbook checks through api-read. The endpoints themselves stay: the pages and the nextseek-validate-upload op call them directly.
post_port_changes.why: Advertising a read the tool behind the gate refuses costs the agent one of its two attempts on every file download or workbook check (2026-09-18 review, M5).
